Rail and roads · Export corridors

The state of your emprise before the works, and what changes during them

Before a railway is rehabilitated or a road widened, you need to know what stands inside the emprise, how far from the centre line and since when. We record structures, tracks and earthworks by distance band and by segment, at the date that matters to the project, then show what changes while the works run. From satellite imagery, with no access to the works site, and checked by an analyst.

Request a proposal What the texts say

The context

Corridors rehabilitated through emprises occupied for years

The Katanga export corridors, the railways and roads to the ports and to neighbouring countries, are the subject of concession contracts and rehabilitation programmes, including a thirty-year rail concession signed in August 2026 (zoom-eco, 26 August 2026). These projects run through emprises that have been occupied for a long time; where a lender finances them, its resettlement standards call for a census closed at a cut-off date.

The same need arises on roads, where a project can widen its emprise partway through and redefine its cut-off date, and on fibre-optic cables laid in road emprises.

No link with AfriScan

The projects mentioned on this page are public programmes, cited for context. They imply no relationship with AfriScan.

What the texts say

Railway and road emprises

Checked against the published texts on 27 September 2026. A summary of the public rules for orientation; it is not legal advice.

Arrêté interministériel n° 0021 of 29 October 1993 lists among the servitudes:

  • “les emprises des chemins de fer de 5 à 50 mètres suivant catégories”, railway emprises of 5 to 50 metres by category;
  • road emprises, “conformément aux plans d’urbanisme et plans cadastraux”, in line with town-planning and cadastral plans;
  • riverbanks, “jusqu’au moins 10 mètres”, to at least 10 metres.

It prohibits “toute occupation, toute construction et tout lotissement” there, any occupation, construction or subdivision (art. 2). We found no published railway law that sets these widths more precisely.

Near mines, the Mining Code also bars a mining right holder from occupying, without the consent of the competent authorities, land “réservé au projet de chemin de fer”, reserved for a railway project, or a road (art. 279). That rule protects the line against mining occupation; it is not a servitude of the line.

Who decides

Whether a structure is permitted is for you and the competent authorities to decide. A line’s category, and so the width of its emprise, should be confirmed with the line’s manager or with counsel.

When the emprise or the timetable changes

A cut-off date can be redefined; the imagery records each date

A resettlement plan published in January 2025 for a 150 km road financed by the World Bank shows how a project evolves:

  • the cut-off date was set at 13 November 2021, then 6 March 2023, then 15 August 2024;
  • the 2021 and 2023 plans used a 9 m emprise;
  • the August 2024 update widened the emprise to 15 m over the first ten kilometres, and the remaining 140 km are to be updated to 15 m, or 12 m in constrained areas.

The same document defines the cut-off date as “la date qui marque le début de l’opération de recensement des personnes et de leurs biens”, the date that marks the start of the census of people and their assets, after which assets put in place “ne sont pas indemnisés”, are not compensated. A dated image survey keeps a record of what existed at each date; if the width changes, the register is measured again against the new emprise.

The register at the cut-off date

A dated register of the structures in the emprise, at the cut-off date, for the census and asset inventory of a resettlement action plan (RAP).

What you receive

From the baseline register to monitoring the works

The emprise register

Each structure found in the emprise and in a band around it, with its distance from the centre line, its band, its chainage and its coordinates, and every 500 m segment rated for encroachment density.

Route options

Structures counted side by side along each option for a diversion or a new section, to weigh the land impact before the route is fixed.

The cut-off date

A register made at a known date, with IDs, coordinates and the image date, then the changes between the cut-off date and the census.

Progress on the works

Drone orthophotos and elevation models compared from one visit to the next, with the cut and fill areas, subject to the approvals and security clearances each job requires.

Third-party works

Fresh excavations, spoil, trenches and earthworks on or near the emprise and along cable routes, flagged from one survey to the next to show patrols where to look.

Changes

New or removed structures between two surveys, flagged automatically and confirmed by an analyst, with before and after views.

Delivered as a PDF report and GeoPackage, GeoJSON, KMZ and Shapefile files. The same method, for every country: rail and roads · change detection.

What we do, and what we don't

An honest scope

What we do

  • Record the structures, tracks and earthworks visible in and around the emprise
  • Establish a register at a known date, then track the changes
  • Compare route options
  • Work remotely, with no access to the works site

What we don’t do

  • Stand in for a land surveyor’s topographic survey or a measurement of quantities
  • See underground or detect theft
  • Decide whether a structure is permitted
  • Stand in for the census or the asset inventory

Frequently asked questions

What emprise width do you use for a railway?

The one that applies to your line. Arrêté interministériel n° 0021 of 29 October 1993 sets railway emprises “de 5 à 50 mètres suivant catégories”, from 5 to 50 metres by category. Tell us the width the line’s manager or the project uses; we can measure up to six distances in one survey.

And for a road?

For roads, the 1993 arrêté refers to town-planning and cadastral plans. In practice the width is often the project’s own: a resettlement plan published for a World Bank-financed road moved from a 9 m emprise to a 15 m one on its first 10 km, with the rest to be updated at 15 m, or 12 m in constrained areas.

Can you track progress on the works?

Yes. Dated drone orthophotos and elevation models are compared from one visit to the next, with the cut and fill areas. Drone surveys are subject to the approvals and security clearances each job requires. It does not stand in for a land surveyor’s topographic survey or a measurement of quantities.

Do you detect damage to cables laid in the emprise?

No. We flag fresh excavations, trenches and earthworks visible at the surface on or near a cable route, to show patrols where to look. We cannot see underground, and we detect neither theft nor damage.

Can your register stand in for the census of affected people?

No. It establishes what existed at a known date and supports the census and asset inventory; it does not replace them and records no one.

Send us your railway or road route

The route (KML, KMZ, Shapefile, GeoJSON or GeoPackage), the emprise width used, the province and the date the register must reflect. We reply with a scope, an imagery plan and a written proposal.
